authority: CEO Round 84 deep audit directive: 'make constitutive equivalence a gate. The orchestrator should refuse L3 if material_label_same = true but constitutive_equations_verified = false. That is a hard gate.'

gate_rule.name: Constitutive-Equivalence Hard Gate
gate_rule.formula: L3_permitted = (strain_energy_density_equivalent AND stress_law_equivalent AND compressibility_formulation_equivalent AND parameter_mapping_equivalent AND stress_measure_equivalent AND quadrature_equivalent AND reference_configuration_equivalent)
gate_rule.shortcut_refusal: If material_label_same = true BUT any of the seven equivalence checks above = false, L3 is REFUSED. The material label is NOT evidence of constitutive equivalence.
shortcut_refusal_examples: FEBio 'neo-Hookean' uses W_vol = (K/2)(ln J)^2; SfePy 'dw_tl_bulk_penalty' uses W_vol = (K/2)(J-1)^2. Both labeled 'neo-Hookean', but volumetric SED differs. REFUSED.
FEBio outputs Cauchy stress; SfePy 'term_mode=stress' outputs 2nd Piola-Kirchhoff stress. Same model, different stress measure. REFUSED until both pushed forward / pulled back to same measure.
FEBio default quadrature for hex8 is 2x2x2 Gauss; SfePy Integral('i', order=2) gives 2x2x2 Gauss. Same — OK.

1_strain_energy_density.description: Both solvers must use the SAME mathematical form of W(C, J). The functional form (including all invariants, exponents, and dependencies) must be identical, not just 'similar'.
1_strain_energy_density.audit_method: Write down the actual W function from each solver's source/manual, side by side. Check character-by-character equivalence of the mathematical expression.
common_violations: (K/2)(ln J)^2 vs (K/2)(J-1)^2  — logarithmic vs quadratic volumetric penalty
Mooney-Rivlin W = C1(I1-3) + C2(I2-3) vs neo-Hookean W = (mu/2)(I1-3)  — different terms even if 'similar'
Ogden W = sum_i (mu_i/alpha_i)(lambda_1^alpha_i + lambda_2^alpha_i + lambda_3^alpha_i - 3) vs neo-Hookean  — different functional form

2_stress_law.description: Both solvers must derive stress from W via the SAME formula. For hyperelasticity, S = 2 dW/dC is standard, but variations exist.
2_stress_law.audit_method: Compare the stress formula in each solver's documentation/source.
common_violations: S = 2 dW/dC (standard) vs S = dW/dE (where E = (C-I)/2; equivalent if consistent, but watch for missing factors)
Deviatoric-volumetric split (S = S_dev + S_vol) vs single-form S — must be algebraically equivalent

3_compressibility_formulation.description: For compressible materials, both solvers must use the SAME volumetric law. This is where 'neo-Hookean' labels diverge most often.
3_compressibility_formulation.audit_method: Identify the volumetric term in each solver's W. Compare formulas directly.
common_violations: Pure displacement formulation with penalty (K/2)(J-1)^2
Mixed u-p formulation with (K/2)(ln J)^2
Sussman-Bathe mixed formulation
Three-field (F-bar) formulation

4_parameter_mapping.description: If the solvers accept different input parameters (E, nu vs mu, K vs C1, C2), the mapping must be exact and documented.
4_parameter_mapping.audit_method: Write down each solver's input parameters. Compute the mapping. Verify by substitution.
common_violations: E = 2mu(1+nu) vs E = 3mu(1-2nu) — first is correct, second is for pure shear, different physical regime
K = E/(3(1-2nu)) vs K = E/(2(1+nu)) — second is actually mu, not K
Ogden parameters mu_i, alpha_i vs Mooney-Rivlin C1, C2 — mapping is non-trivial

5_stress_measure.description: Both solvers must output stress in the SAME measure (Cauchy, 2nd PK, 1st PK, etc.). If different, the push-forward / pull-back transformation must be explicitly applied and verified.
5_stress_measure.audit_method: Identify the stress measure each solver outputs. If different, derive and apply the transformation.
common_violations: FEBio VTK 'stress' = Cauchy; SfePy 'term_mode=stress' = 2nd PK  — must push SfePy forward
Some FEBio materials output Kirchhoff stress tau = J*sigma  — must divide by J
Engineering strain vs Green strain  — different conjugate stress measures

6_quadrature.description: Both solvers must use the SAME numerical integration rule. For hex8, this is typically 2x2x2 Gauss (8 points) but other options exist.
6_quadrature.audit_method: Check each solver's integration order setting for the same element type.
common_violations: Full 2x2x2 Gauss vs reduced 1-point integration  — different locking behavior
Selectively reduced integration (B-bar method) vs uniform integration
Different Gauss point locations (Legendre vs Chebyshev)

7_reference_configuration.description: Both solvers must use the SAME reference configuration. For Total Lagrangian (TL), this is the undeformed geometry. For Updated Lagrangian (UL), this is the current deformed geometry.
7_reference_configuration.audit_method: Identify the formulation type for each solver. TL and UL are mathematically equivalent but require different bookkeeping.
common_violations: TL formulation integrating over Omega_0 vs UL formulation integrating over Omega_t  — equivalent if implemented correctly, but if outputs are taken at different times/steps, comparison is invalid
Reference temperature for thermal expansion  — must match

gate_enforcement.audit_frequency: Before every L3 cross-solver comparison attempt
gate_enforcement.audit_artifact_required: Each L3 attempt must include a CONSTITUTIVE_EQUIVALENCE_AUDIT.json file alongside the L3 result. The audit must explicitly answer all seven checks. If any check is 'false' or 'unknown', L3 is REFUSED.
gate_enforcement.refusal_action: If gate refuses L3, the orchestrator must NOT proceed with cross-solver comparison. Either (a) reconfigure one solver to match the other, OR (b) re-derive the analytical reference for BOTH formulations and compare each solver against its matching analytical reference.

sfepy_audit.2_stress_law: S = mu*J^(-2/3)*(I - (1/3)*tr(C)*C^-1) + K*(J-1)*J*C^-1  [verified from SfePy source]
sfepy_audit.5_stress_measure: SfePy 'term_mode=stress' = 2nd Piola-Kirchhoff. MUST push forward to Cauchy via sigma = (1/J) F S F^T before comparison.

applied_to_L3-BENCHMARK-002.febio_audit_PENDING: FEBio binary was wiped between sessions. When rebuilt, the audit must be completed BEFORE any L3 run. Key risk: FEBio's default 'neo-Hookean' material uses (K/2)(ln J)^2 volumetric SED, which FAILS check #1 against this benchmark. Resolution options: (a) use FEBio's uncoupled neo-Hookean with custom volumetric, (b) use FEBio user material plugin, (c) re-freeze benchmark to use (ln J)^2 volumetric.

lessons_encoded: CE-020: Material label 'neo-Hookean' is NOT evidence of constitutive equivalence. FEBio uses (K/2)(ln J)^2 volumetric; SfePy uses (K/2)(J-1)^2. These differ by ~10% in stress at J=1.04 and ~58% at J=1.2. Round 82-83 L3 attempts were comparing non-equivalent models. This gate prevents recurrence.
